subtitle: Lesson 18 · Core ITIL 4 Practices: Incident, Problem & Change

code:
Monday, 8:40am: checkout discount codes fail
for ~20% of transactions. Reps calling in.

This is the 4th time this month. Each time:
restart the discount-pricing microservice,
errors stop for a few days, then return.
caption: A real-shaped scenario, no ServiceNow instance required.

eyebrow: Walking it through all three practices

steps.label: Incident management
steps.sub: log, triage by impact x urgency, escalate to the known fast fix, restore service

steps.label: Problem management
steps.sub: 4th occurrence triggers investigation; root cause is a memory leak; known error logged

steps.label: Change enablement
steps.sub: the code fix is a normal change — assessed, authorized, scheduled for a quiet window

code:
Workaround already in place (restart)
        +
No active outage right now
        =
Time for full risk assessment -> normal change

(If there were no workaround and an outage
was live, this could instead be an
emergency change — still authorized, just fast.)
caption: Emergency vs. normal depends on whether the business can wait, not on how severe the root cause sounds.
